extraction_status.description: OK = every field resolved from the inputs. INCOMPLETE = one or more fields could not be resolved and were left absent. DEGRADED = a config/schema/tool the skill depends on was unavailable. Never OK when extraction_gaps is non-empty.

extraction_gaps.description: Everything the skill could NOT resolve, written instead of guessing a value. Empty array = clean extraction.

field.description: JSON path of the unresolved field, e.g. business_requirements[3].target_module. Use 'ENVIRONMENT' for install/tool failures not tied to one field.

reason.description: Why it could not be resolved, citing the source section checked.

action.description: What a human must do to close the gap.

severity.description: BLOCKING = schema-required field absent. DEGRADED = resolved without normal grounding. WARN = structural inconsistency detected but output emitted (e.g. connector parity drift). INFO = optional content genuinely absent from the source.

app.description: ADDITION. App this context belongs to. Optional, but sdet-plan-generator keys off it to match contexts for a run, so omitting it in a multi-app split defeats the split.

design_source.description: ADDITION. Provenance from the figma-design-bundle manifest and per-state Raw JSON export envelope (file/page, scope, counts, geometry flags). Lets a reviewer tell a full-page export from a partial selection export without live design access.

scope.description: envelope scope. 'selection' means flows leaving the selected layers are not in the export, so ui_flow coverage cannot be verified.

truncated_count.description: envelope export.truncatedCount. Non-zero means the depth cap dropped children — elements below those layers were never exported.

has_geometry.description: Whether the export carried x/y/width/height. False means board nodes were classified by the descendant-count proxy instead of by size, and lane-entry resolution was unavailable.

truncated_nodes.description: envelope export.truncatedNodes (up to 20 samples) — the layers worth flattening before the next export.

visual_analysis_scratchpad.description: Write a 2-3 sentence overview of what you detect in the export before compiling the technical fields. List screens found. Note: the export carries frame size and position but no styling, so this is a structural reading of names, variants, reactions and frame size — not a visual one.

screen_id.description: Figma frame title forced into UPPER_SNAKE_CASE (e.g., LOGIN_SCREEN). Any trailing state/locale qualifier is stripped and the BASE name kept — 'Confirm account / EN' is CONFIRM_ACCOUNT with 'EN' as a state, never EN.

source_ref.description: ADDITION. Figma node id of the representative frame (e.g. '1997:31939'), so a reviewer can jump straight to it.

source_refs.description: ADDITION. Every frame collapsed into this screen. A screen drawn as N sibling state-frames has N ids here, and a connector touching ANY of them resolves to this screen — resolving against source_ref alone silently drops the flows drawn from the other states.

node_class.description: ADDITION. How the board-node classifier labelled this frame. Only SCREEN entries belong in screens[]; another value appears only when an unresolved classification was recorded for review.

classified_by.description: ADDITION. Which test decided the class. GEOMETRY is the normal case; DESCENDANT_COUNT means the export carried no size and the proxy was used, paired with a DEGRADED gap.

purpose.description: OPTIONAL, no longer produced. A Figma board carries no purpose statement, and nothing downstream reads this field, so the extractor does not emit it and its absence is never a gap. Kept defined so hand-authored contexts stay valid.

deep_link.description: ADDITION, optional. Deep link opening this screen, from a prototype URL action matching the app config's deeplink_scheme or a Note/Context note stating one. Most designs document no routing: absence is normal, never a gap, and never a constructed URI.

entry_point.description: ADDITION. True when this frame is named in the page's flowStartingPoints[].

screen_states.description: State variants of this screen, in the designer's own wording. When N sibling frames share a base name, the entries are their QUALIFIERS ('EN', 'Error', 'Filled') — never the base name repeated N times, which carries no information.

state_kinds.description: ADDITION. screen_states normalised to a fixed vocabulary, so downstream category selection is a mechanical field check rather than free-text pattern matching.

element_id.description: Logical element id: <SCREEN_ID>.<purpose><role_suffix>[.<state>] — UPPER_SNAKE screen half, lower_snake role half (e.g. CONFIRM_ACCOUNT.approve_btn). Bundle extraction assigns ids via scripts/design_extractor heuristics (aligned with config naming_convention in docs); config element_id_pattern is not applied at runtime. Join key to change_context; do not re-case or hand-edit after extraction.

source_ref.description: ADDITION. Figma node id of this layer.

role.description: ADDITION. Normalised role. Machine-readable companion to `type`; downstream uses it to decide whether a screen is interactive without pattern-matching free text.

accessibility_id.description: ADDITION, optional. Accessibility/test id the designer happened to write into a Dev Mode annotation, transcribed verbatim. Most files carry no annotations: absence is the normal case, never a gap, and never derived from the layer name.

platform_hints.description: ADDITION, optional. Per-platform ids when an annotation states them separately. Omit entirely otherwise — never a placeholder.

interactions.description: One entry per connector leaving this element — a trigger with two connectors gets two entries. A connector whose endpoint is a NOTE produces no entry: an annotation tether is not behaviour, and its text belongs in validations_and_edge_cases instead.

action.description: Readable on its own, without cross-referencing ui_flow: names the destination and the connector it came from.

connector_id.description: ADDITION. Figma node id of the connector this interaction came from.

destination_node_id.description: ADDITION. The literal connectorEnd.endpointNodeId — the layer the arrow actually lands on, which is often a caption or label rather than a frame. Present whenever the connector is attached; absent for a floating endpoint. This is the id to paste into Figma.

destination_screen_id.description: ADDITION. The RESOLVED destination screen, which frequently differs from destination_node_id. Absent when the endpoint resolves to a decision box, to a caption fronting no distinct screen, or back to this element's own screen — the same self-loop guard ui_flow applies, so the two halves of the file never disagree.

element_ambiguity.description: ADDITION. Per-element confidence, when this element is less certain than the screen overall.

ui_flow.description: Ordered breadth-first from the flow's entry point(s): ENTRY edges first, then each reached screen's outgoing edges wave by wave, then edges of components unreachable from any entry (appended deterministically by board position). Order is presentational — no consumer may attach semantics to array position beyond readability.

from_screen_id.description: Screen id, or the reserved pseudo-node 'ENTRY' (statechart initial-state pattern): an ENTRY edge marks where the flow starts. 'ENTRY' never appears in screens[], is valid only as from_screen_id, and only on edges whose edge_source is ENTRY_LABEL or ENTRY_TOPOLOGY. Scripts emit it; the enrichment pass never touches it.

trigger_element_id.description: The element that triggers the transition. OMIT the key entirely for a frame-to-frame connector with no identifiable trigger — never emit null, and never invent a token to satisfy the schema.

trigger_source_ref.description: ADDITION. Figma node id of the element layer that triggered this transition. Present when trigger_element_id is set. Disambiguates canonical element_ids shared across state-variant twins (multiple screens[].elements[] rows with the same element_id but different source_ref). Join key for automation: match trigger_source_ref to screens[].elements[].source_ref.

condition.description: The connector's label (standard #4). For a contracted branch this is COMPOSED, not copied: '<decision question> — <value>' (e.g. 'Does user have GoPay+? — YES'), with any label on the connector into the decision kept in front via ' / '. Empty string means unconditional.

decision_question.description: ADDITION, contracted edges only. The decision box's question, whitespace-normalised (a designer's 'Does user have GoPay+ ?' becomes 'Does user have GoPay+?'). Lets a consumer build a precondition without re-parsing `condition`.

decision_value.description: ADDITION, contracted edges only. The branch this edge takes — the exit connector's label, e.g. YES / NO.

decision_node_id.description: ADDITION, contracted edges only. Figma node id of the decision box, so a reviewer can see why the condition attached where it did.

navigation_kind.description: ADDITION. SWAP / CHANGE_TO / SCROLL_TO reactions are element state changes, not navigation, and never appear as ui_flow edges. ENTRY is used only on edges from the reserved ENTRY pseudo-node.

edge_source.description: ADDITION. Where the edge came from. _INFERRED means the destination was derived rather than drawn. CONNECTOR_CONTRACTED means a decision box between two screens was collapsed so its condition could attach to the screen it belongs to; source_ref holds the EXIT connector (the one carrying the branch label), consistent with every other edge, and the box itself is in decision_node_id. ENTRY_LABEL / ENTRY_TOPOLOGY appear only on edges from the reserved ENTRY pseudo-node: ENTRY_LABEL = an explicit designer signal (an 'Entry point' / '1st time' qualifier on a screen label chip, or a prototype flow starting point; source_ref = the chip/frame node id), ENTRY_TOPOLOGY = inferred from graph topology when the board carries no explicit label (zero in-degree root with the widest forward reach; source_ref = the screen's frame id).

edge_direction_source.description: ADDITION, present only when direction was NOT the plain case. The arrowhead defines flow direction, not the order the line was drawn: ARROWHEAD_REVERSED means the arrow sits on connectorStart and the edge was emitted swapped. AMBIGUOUS = arrows both ends; UNDIRECTED = neither. Absent means the ordinary ARROWHEAD case.

from_source_ref.description: ADDITION. Figma node id of connectorStart.endpointNodeId — the exact node the connector arrow starts from. Cross-reference with screens[].source_ref to find the originating screen object. Omitted for ENTRY pseudo-edges (no connector start).

to_source_ref.description: ADDITION. Figma node id of connectorEnd.endpointNodeId — the exact node the connector arrow lands on. Cross-reference with screens[].source_ref to find the destination screen object.

source_ref.description: ADDITION. Figma node id of the connector, or of the node carrying the reaction.
